codeReview.summary: Fail with one blocking issue. The feature adds first-class `flux apps health|logs|inspect|stats|top|monitor|exec|test-install` routing, produces structured summaries with resource-backed large outputs, and gives `exec`/`test-install` explicit status fields. However, the semantic reducer used by `test-install` still prefers the last parsed JSON object's `status: success` over later plain-text error events, so a mixed progress stream can be reported as successful even after the install has actually failed. That breaks VAL-APPS-006's requirement to determine success from meaningful operation results rather than HTTP status alone.

issues.description: `deriveProgressSemantic` returns success immediately when the last parsed JSON object has `status: success` (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:4971-4980`) before it checks whether later plain-text events report an error (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:4995-5009`). `parseProgressOutput` preserves later trailing text as ordered events in MCP (`flux-mcp/src/index.ts:355-418`), and `handleAppsTestInstall` trusts that semantic result for top-level `ok`/`status` and exit code (`fluxos-cli/src/cli.ts:6592-6626`). As a result, a stream like a success JSON object followed by `error: ...` would still exit as success even though the meaningful final progress state is failure. The new tests only cover pure-success and pure-failure cases (`fluxos-cli/test/apps-runtime-debug-exec.test.ts:544-568`), so this mixed-stream regression is not covered.
